title: What's the deal with crop circles?
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant examine crop circles: the Led Zeppelin box set joke, early historical claims (the 1678 mowing devil woodcut, John Rand Capron's 1880 Nature letter), the 1970s-80s origin of the modern hoax by Doug Bauer and Dave Chorley in Southern England, how designs grew more complex (Julia set, fractals), believer theories (aliens, Gerald Hawkins' claimed new geometry), skeptic and natural explanations (plasma vortex, Terence Meaden, microwave heating per William Levengood and Richard Taylor, wind and helicopter downdrafts), how crop circles are made with ropes and planks, commercial crop circle makers, and skeptic debunking points by Joe Nickell. Ends with a listener mail about a Chilean saying.

segments.title: Opening banter and Led Zeppelin crop circle joke
segments.summary: Hosts joke about snowshoes and a Led Zeppelin box set cover showing a crop circle, then say crop circles are a hoax that is art, not aliens.

segments.title: Early history: mowing devil and 1880 Nature report
segments.summary: The mowing devil woodcut from the seventeenth century is discussed as supposed early evidence, along with John Rand Capron's report in Nature about a wheat field apparently flattened by cyclonic wind.

segments.title: Origin of modern hoax by Doug Bauer and Dave Chorley
segments.summary: The modern hoax began in the 1970s after a UFO-linked circle in Australia; Doug Bauer and a friend started making crop circles in southern England, and sloped-field designs made the phenomenon take off.

segments.title: Growth, designs, and Gerald Hawkins' geometry claims
segments.summary: Crop circles became a tourist attraction in the 1990s and grew more complex, paired with paranoid 1990s culture and The X-Files. Gerald Hawkins, a retired astronomer, claimed a new Euclidean geometry, which the hosts say was never recognized by mathematicians.

segments.title: Locations, field types, and the Oliver's Castle video
segments.summary: Most crop circles are in Hampshire and Wiltshire in southern England near Stonehenge. Corn, oat, barley and tobacco fields are used. The Oliver's Castle video is discussed, and its maker later said it was faked with computer programs.

segments.title: Theories: aliens, plasma vortex, wind, microwaves
segments.summary: Theories covered include alien messages, the plasma vortex theory of Terence Meaden, helicopter downdrafts, magnetic and electromagnetic radiation claims, and biophysicist William Levengood's microwave heating idea, with Richard Taylor's magnetron explanation. The Julia set and reported menstrual cycle effects are also mentioned as unverified claims.

segments.title: How crops circles are made and the hoax confession
segments.summary: Evidence such as tractor tracks and missing footprints is discussed. Dave Chorley and Doug Bauer went public on the BBC and Good Morning America, showing the rope and plank method. Commercial circle makers were paid for corporate designs, and skeptic debunking points are listed, including Joe Nickell's four points.

segments.title: Wrap-up on crop circles as art
segments.summary: The hosts call crop circles art and mention the Nasca lines and designs such as the Mothman, and sign off inviting listeners to learn more.

segments.title: Listener mail: Chilean camouflage saying
segments.summary: A listener named Matt writes about a Chilean saying about experts who neglect their expertise at home, which the hosts compare to the cobbler's children saying.
